title: CRASH-083: call user func params into argument stack invalidated by autoload realloc uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1902 in zif_call_user_func when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 8bd18e174b4e, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1885 (defect: full params[] fetched before zend_is_callable); fault observed at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1902
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build crashes on it natively, so a silence on an arm is not a MISSED: under the judge's default scoring the case reads out-of-denominator on every arm; the sensitivity scoring (run-realphp.py --score-oracle-crashes) reads it by fault site instead.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has zif_call_user_func at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:1902 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the nested allocator layer retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)
virtual-nested-exact.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: NOT-REISSUED: no capability fault at the platform default, but the eager configuration (runtime_revocation_every_free_default=1) faults on this case, so the stale pointer IS followed. The eager fault lands inside the script body, which is what tells a revoked object apart from the allocator's cache being drained back to libc at shutdown. Context, not a verdict: every-free also faults on accesses nothing is meant to catch; out-of-denominator under the default scoring: the corpus's pristine record for this case is SIGNAL:11, so the unprotected program dies anyway and there is no pair to read. Run again with --score-oracle-crashes for the reading by fault site
